solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Foil employer who erects barriers?

blocks.note: first meaning: a sportsman who wields a foil, the light sword
second meaning: someone who puts up fences

explanation.surface: A puzzling job description: someone who employs foil, or a builder of barriers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foil' reads as kitchen wrap or a verb meaning thwart; here it is the fencing sword.
explanation.definitionFit: A fencer is both a sword sportsman using a foil and a tradesman who builds fences.

clue.text: English educational foundation embraces old fallacy

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold something within your arms, so one piece wraps round another

blocks.note: E is the standard abbreviation for English
the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic, are the basics of education
O is a common abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An English school trust clings to an outdated mistaken belief.
explanation.walkthrough: The O sits between the second and third R of the three Rs.
explanation.definitionFit: A fallacy is a mistaken belief, which is a kind of error.

clue.text: Like novelist, runs into accountant who was unbelievably accurate?

indicators.note: going into something means being placed inside it, so these letters sit within the accountant

blocks.note: CA is a chartered accountant
as Sand: George Sand was the French novelist
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A novelist-like figure barges into an accountant with uncanny precision.
explanation.walkthrough: AS SAND plus R goes inside CA. 'Unbelievably' carries the joke: Cassandra's prophecies were true but never believed.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Cassandra foretold the future correctly but was cursed so that nobody believed her.

clue.text: One of four men initially on board that is neophyte

blocks.clueFragment: One of four men initially on board
blocks.note: a chess set has four rooks, standing in the corners at the start
i.e. stands for id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: One of four new recruits on a company board is a beginner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That is' does double service: 'that' plus the link 'is' read as i.e.; the board is a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookie is a raw beginner, just as a neophyte is a newcomer to something.

clue.text: Ill after start of fast? Get medicine here

indicators.note: placed after just the opening letter, these letters go inside the word near its front

blocks.note: pacy means quick
ill as a noun is harm

explanation.surface: Feeling unwell after beginning a fast, you head for the chemist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like going without food, but it is the adjective, quick.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacy is the shop where prescribed drugs are dispensed, so it is where you obtain medicine.

clue.text: How numbers of letters appear here to bring up one demand they oddly put about

definitions.text: How numbers of letters appear here

indicators.note: something done oddly is done in a strange way, so these letters come out jumbled
put about means placed around, so the jumbled letters surround the middle pieces

blocks.note: to parent a child is to bring it up
taken as written, to be rearranged
Roman numeral one
a call is a demand, as in a call for action

explanation.surface: A rambling instruction about raising someone and demanding they act strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter count of every clue, like (15) here, is printed in brackets, so it appears this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Enumerations sit in parentheses after each clue, so the numbers are shown in brackets, an apt self-referential definition.

clue.text: Even if a learner pondered, not reaching conclusion

indicators.note: stopping short of the conclusion means the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the learner plate on a British car
thought, meaning pondered, without its final letter

explanation.surface: A student mulled it over without ever reaching a conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Although and even if are synonymous conjunctions introducing a concession.

clue.text: After short time, like fiddle that's taken up theme

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: a mo is a moment
from the idiom 'fit as a fiddle'

explanation.surface: After a moment, a violin is picked up to play its main tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' suggests the violin or a swindle; the idiom fit as a fiddle supplies the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A motif is a recurring idea or musical figure, which is what a theme is.

clue.text: Eccentric co-stars in part of Breakfast at Tiffany's

indicators.note: eccentric means off-centre and odd, so the letters are thrown out of their normal order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Quirky co-stars appear in the famous Audrey Hepburn film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' does double duty as fodder; the film opens with Holly Golightly eating a pastry outside Tiffany's window.
explanation.definitionFit: The film title is taken literally: a croissant is a typical item of a breakfast.

clue.text: Star actor I recast as Dracula, say

indicators.note: to recast is to cast again in a new form, so the letters take new places

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A leading actor says he has been recast to play the vampire.
explanation.definitionFit: Count Dracula holds a noble title, so he is an example of a nobleman.

clue.text: Kind of weight that a horse finally brought down

definitions.text: that a horse finally brought down

blocks.note: first meaning: the system of weights used for precious metals

blocks.clueFragment: that a horse finally brought down
blocks.note: second meaning: the city that fell to the wooden horse of the Greeks

explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' tempts you to take a last letter; it just means at the end of a ten-year siege.
explanation.definitionFit: Troy weight measures gold and silver, and Troy was the ancient city destroyed after the Trojan horse ruse.

clue.text: Split personality, for example, in tattered raincoat

indicators.note: something tattered is ragged and torn apart, so the letters are scattered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A person with a split personality wanders about in a shabby mac.
explanation.walkthrough: Split is a city in Croatia, so a personality from there is one native.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone notable from the Croatian city of Split is a citizen of Croatia.

clue.text: Love one part of school that's stupid

blocks.note: love is nil in tennis, shaped like O
a school is a shoal, and one member is a fish

explanation.surface: A sweetheart who is in one class at school turns out to be dim.
explanation.definitionFit: Oafish describes a clumsy, dull-witted person, so it fits stupid as an adjective.

clue.text: Surrounded by maidens, surrounded by helping hands

indicators.note: being surrounded means being enclosed, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: aid is help, as given by helping hands
in cricket scoring M stands for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Someone is surrounded by young women, who are all lending a hand.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden over in cricket is one in which no runs are scored.
explanation.definitionFit: Amid is a preposition meaning in the middle of, the same as surrounded by.

clue.text: Visitor to China has nothing to pack up before game

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: nothing is zero, shaped like O
to cram is to pack tightly
polo is a game played on horseback

explanation.surface: A traveller to China has no need to pack before a match.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian merchant Marco Polo famously travelled to the court of Kublai Khan in China.

clue.text: The main challenges for sopranos, as you can hear

indicators.note: what you can hear is what is spoken, so the sound counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: top Cs are hard notes for sopranos to reach

explanation.surface: Sopranos' main difficulties lie in their top notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' reads as 'the chief', but the main is an old word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a poetic term for the ocean, and the high seas are the open ocean.

clue.text: In part, take French or Spanish translation for the anthology

indicators.note: putting something in a word places it inside that word

blocks.note: a section is a part

blocks.clueFragment: take French or Spanish translation for
blocks.note: 'the' is le in French and el in Spanish; the Spanish word fits

explanation.surface: Part of a reading list asks you to translate some French or Spanish for an anthology.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'the' before anthology is the word to be translated; French LE reversed would also do.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthology is a selection of poems or stories chosen from various works.

clue.text: Saint subject to criticism? That's child's play

blocks.note: St Peter the apostle
a pan is a harsh review

explanation.surface: A saint exposed to criticism shrugs it off as easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Child's play' usually means something easy; here it is literally a play for children.
explanation.definitionFit: J M Barrie's Peter Pan is a stage play written for children.

clue.text: Old soldier turning in torn decoration

indicators.note: turning round means facing the other way, so the soldier is read backwards
placed in something means put inside it

blocks.note: O is a common abbreviation for old
a man is a private soldier, as in officers and men
rent is the past tense of rend, to tear

explanation.surface: An old soldier turns up wearing a ripped medal.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornament is a decoration, something added to make a thing look attractive.

clue.text: Being behind, with others going back

indicators.note: going back means running the other way, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: et al. is Latin for 'and others'

explanation.surface: Behind schedule, with everyone else heading home.
explanation.definitionFit: Late means behind time, arriving after you should.

clue.text: Put the lid on strong drink

blocks.note: first meaning: to put an end to, as with a rumour
second meaning: whisky from Scotland

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests closing a bottle of spirits; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a plan is to stop it, and Scotch is whisky, a strong spirit.

clue.text: Spirits raised after swallowing a litre

indicators.note: swallowing something takes it inside, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: raised, as in increased, means more
a, plus L for litre

explanation.surface: Drinkers' spirits rise after they knock back a whole litre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirits raised' looks like a single phrase; only 'Spirits' defines, in the sense of mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Morale is a group's confidence and mood, their spirits in the sense of state of mind.

clue.text: Former American student briefly holding British record

indicators.note: said briefly means cut short, so the end is lopped off
holding something means having it inside

blocks.note: alumnus, a graduate in US usage, shortened
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A US graduate is in briefly to hold a British record.
explanation.definitionFit: An album is a long-playing record of several tracks.

clue.text: Dawn to stand up and boast

blocks.note: to cock is to turn up, as with ears or a hat
to crow is to brag

explanation.surface: Someone rises at daybreak to brag about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockcrow is the time when roosters crow, an old word for early morning.

clue.text: Further letters after one or two from female or male relative

indicators.text: letters after one or two from
indicators.note: keeping only what follows the first one or two letters drops the start

blocks.note: mother, or equally brother, both end the same way

explanation.surface: More characters are added after those of a male or female relation.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping M from mother or BR from brother leaves the same word, hence 'one or two'.
explanation.definitionFit: Other means additional or further, as in 'other examples'.

clue.text: Grave situation from doctor's perspective

blocks.note: a situation seen from a point of view is 'to' someone
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor's view of a patient's state is that it is serious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' reads as serious; it is the noun. 'To MB' is how a situation looks to a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A grave is a burial place, and a tomb is a vault for the dead.

clue.text: One group in difficulty that's always ready to ignite

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase for a noun: the thing that is always ready

indicators.note: placed in something means put inside it

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
a lot is a group or batch
a plight is a predicament

explanation.surface: One band in trouble is always fired up.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot light is a small flame kept burning in a boiler so the burner can be lit at any time.

clue.text: Overeat a lot around a time for celebration

indicators.note: going around something encloses it

blocks.note: to hog is to eat greedily
many means a lot
taken as written

explanation.surface: People stuff themselves heavily at a festive season.
explanation.walkthrough: Hogmanay is the Scottish New Year's Eve celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogmanay is New Year's Eve in Scotland, famous for its parties.

clue.text: Like unsatisfied consumer taking article from European country

indicators.note: taking something from a word removes it

blocks.note: a is the indefinite article
the central European state

explanation.surface: A disgruntled shopper removes an item from Hungary.
explanation.definitionFit: A consumer, in the sense of an eater, who is not satisfied is still wanting food.
